requirement: Fetch many users concurrently through an async client with a bounded number in flight, skipping missing users and always closing the client, plus a spec-limited AsyncMock fake of that client.
skeleton: Client protocol with async get and aclose, fake_client building a spec_set AsyncMock with an async side_effect, and load_profiles validating limit, gathering semaphore-guarded fetches inside try/finally that awaits aclose.
caption: Concurrent async client code tested against unittest.mock.AsyncMock. Client is a typing.Protocol with async get(path) returning a JSON body or raising LookupError, and async aclose(). fake_client(responses) builds AsyncMock(spec_set=Client), so get and aclose are awaitable child mocks and any other attribute raises AttributeError; get gets an async side_effect that returns the mapped body or raises LookupError naming the path. load_profiles(client, user_ids, limit=2) raises ValueError saying limit must be at least 1 before touching the client. It then fetches /users/<id> for every id with asyncio.gather, each call guarded by an asyncio.Semaphore of size limit, turning LookupError into a skipped user while any other exception, such as RuntimeError, propagates. client.aclose is awaited in a finally block so the pool is released even when a fetch fails, and the result maps each found id to its body. The fixture asserts that users 1 and 3 load while 2 is skipped with assert_has_awaits and one aclose await, that a RuntimeError from get propagates yet aclose is still awaited once, that a tracking side_effect sees at most 3 in flight with limit=3 and at most 2 by default, that limit=-1 raises ValueError without awaiting get, and that the fake rejects client.post and raises LookupError for an unknown path.

rationale.teaches: AsyncMock(spec_set=Protocol) for awaitable children, async side_effect functions, and assert_awaited_once/assert_has_awaits for verifying cleanup and calls.
rationale.why: A MagicMock cannot be awaited and an unspecced AsyncMock accepts any attribute, so async cleanup and concurrency bugs pass tests that never check awaits.

ops.docstring: Test concurrent async client code against an AsyncMock client.

ops.source:
class Client(Protocol):
    """The slice of an HTTP client that load_profiles uses."""

    async def get(self, path: str) -> Body:
        """Return the JSON body at path or raise LookupError."""

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        """Release the connection pool."""

def fake_client(responses: Mapping[str, Body]) -> AsyncMock:
    """An AsyncMock client whose get returns mapped bodies and raises LookupError."""

    async def get(path: str) -> Body:
        if path not in responses:
            raise LookupError(path)
        return responses[path]

    client = AsyncMock(spec_set=Client)
    client.get.side_effect = get
    return client

candidates.why_wrong: Every exception is swallowed as a missing user, hiding real failures.
The client is never closed when a fetch raises.
The default lets three requests run at once instead of two.
A negative limit reaches the Semaphore and fails with the wrong message.
An unspecced AsyncMock accepts attributes the real client does not have.
